Definition: Abigail or Abigal, the name of two Israelitesses
BiblicalUsage: Abigail is ‘a woman of good understanding, and of a beautiful countenance’, the wife of the churlish Nabal. When David marches to kill Nabal’s household, she rides out with provisions, bows before him, and talks him out of bloodguilt; after Nabal’s death she becomes David’s wife and follows him to Hebron. A second Abigail, David's sister, is named in 1 Chronicles 2:16.
TheologicalSignificance: Abigail stops a massacre with bread and a wise speech — and David thanks God for her. I believe she is one of the clearest pictures in Scripture of wisdom in action: she sees the danger, she moves quickly, she speaks truth with humility, and a whole household lives because she did.
